question.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x.$

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{′}\cdot \operatorname{arcoth}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x)^{′}}{{arcoth}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{′}\cdot \operatorname{arcoth}⁡x}{{arcoth}^{2}⁡x}-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x)^{′}}{{arcoth}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{′}}{\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x}-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x)^{′}}{{arcoth}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x}-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{{arcoth}^{2}⁡x}\cdot (\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x}+{{(-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{(1-{x}^{2}){arcoth}^{2}⁡x})}_{⏟}}_{g(x)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)=-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{(1-{x}^{2}){arcoth}^{2}⁡x}.$
